objective: Discover and select the reviewed move's core idea, connect the preparatory change to an intended action and its useful result, and explain realization, interference and necessary costs under owned replies.

constraints.verification: Only these actual-screen cases and focused semantic/ownership checks; no broad regression campaign.
constraints.completion: Text additions, correct incidental facts and passing tests are insufficient. Preserve original failure criteria and report unmet criteria explicitly.

initial_findings: MovePurpose.discover chooses the first candidate and ranks unobserved supported pawn advances ahead of observed uses. Kg2 selected h3; Rf3 selected g3.
firstPurposeResponse can finish after two response classes have returned, without establishing that the selected task is central or even delivered.
ReferencePurposeReading.purposeKnown accepts current contacts as sufficient purpose; scheduler and renderer also supply different root-use evidence.

The existing king-location/check-tempo reader compares immediate opponent moves. The historical Kg2 counterplay needs an intervening central change; extending labels or target lists cannot supply that missing temporal relation.

reference.title: Jacob Aagaard, Grandmaster Preparation: Positional Play
reference.lesson: A useful positional fact is not automatically the main idea. Identify the problem that matters and connect the move and subsequent play to it; the opponent's counterplay can change the required move order.

criteria.Kg2: Explain preparatory king relocation and a concrete later checking-tempo difference associated with central play. Do not substitute g3 support or h3 preparation. Distinguish a conditional legal example from best defense or the cause of a numerical evaluation gap.
criteria.Rf3: Explain the rook's intended activation and why the actual reply changes the required continuation. Preserve the c-pawn/central-knight problem and any material cost in the selected lines. Do not substitute g3 support, arbitrary targets or merely state that its purpose is unknown.
criteria.heldout_Re2: Explain the clearance/coordination behind moving the e1 rook before the a1 rook, and the opponent's realized or preventive reply with its cost. Actual engine comparisons remain authoritative; the historical book is a hypothesis source, not a forced verdict.

heldout_preregistration.hypothesis: Re2 makes room for Rae1 and coordinated e-file play; an early ...Bc6 can offer a different course involving an exchange instead of allowing a free attack. Neither the book's verdict nor its exact continuation is required of Stockfish.

development_findings: Admitting new legal preparation examples changes the packet owner. PV readings must be rebound before projection; the first Kg2 screen returned HTTP 500 at 8.31 seconds when this was missed.

The first Rf3 screen reached the 10-second deadline. A later minimal response removed too much: downstream search requires the exact prefix inventory AND a declared question. Preserve those and omit unrelated future catalogues, not the proof of the next work.

An owned preparation question now connects candidate use, actual root/reference paths and two bounded scopes: the action after the actual reply, and a second legal first reply observed later in the same source PV.
Realization is reread from the original pieces and actual controls under each reply. Equal UCI alone cannot establish that a rook battery or king attack survives a blocker or exchange.
Full-prefix material costs must not seed new escape/clearance stories. Shared completion receives prepared content as meaning sources while all selected capture receipts remain mandatory.

A preparation can retain its function after the acting central piece trades: king preparation tracks the king after starting the central play; a rook battery must retain both physical rooks and its target relationship.
Capturing the attacker is not moving its target. An identical prepared move can also have a different target after a pawn recapture; carry that physical change into the response explanation.

Legality of a later PV reply is not strategic relevance at the root child. The final survey evaluates the complete legal reply pool at that exact owned position and returns the top three; the basic screen uses one additional reply. No additional engine job, depth or node allowance was added.

implementation.shared_model: MoveIntent.Question/Reading/Branch owns the actual assessed root, preparatory change, physical user/partner/target, intended use and its certified legal bridge. Discovery, probe scheduling, completion and rendering consume this reading.
implementation.discovery: A quiet root must itself open the later route. Candidate uses are ranked by independent assessed PV observation before a structural coordination candidate. King preparation searches bounded paired legal histories for the same later checking entry, with pawn capture and checking response retained.
implementation.reply_work: One action comparison after the actual reply and one first-reply survey of the complete legal pool at that exact owned child. Return top three and explain one other reply. D12 and ordinary 2M-node/2.5s allowance; no forced book move or substituted root evaluation. Full legal scope is verified independently on the web boundary.
implementation.function: Reread original pieces, line controls, surviving partner, moved target and blockers. Central-piece exchange does not erase a king preparation; identical rook notation does not prove the same pressure.
implementation.delivery: New question and pending prefix inventories stay attached to issued work and receipts. Child comparisons supplement, never replace, the actual root evaluation pair. Full branch material costs remain mandatory and no longer seed unrelated escape stories. Identical physical capturing alternatives use their already displayed occurrence, while their separate tested comparison remains a proof receipt; this prevents duplicate capture-cost episodes.

remaining_limits: The candidate vocabulary remains bounded to prepared activation/coordination and delayed checking-tempo examples. This does not discover every long plan or rank all strategic ideas by human importance.
A legal checking-tempo bridge is conditional; it does not prove best defense, the book sacrifice, or the full numerical evaluation cause.
Response and function claims end at named observed checkpoints. A blocked or postponed plan can become available later; no permanent impossibility is asserted.

Repeated small-search PVs and move classifications vary. Current real assessment pair remains authoritative. One Re2 development run needed 9.56 seconds; broad 10-second stability is unproven. The first job after the final survey update stopped at 10.01s even though the next Re2 job completed at 6.05s.
Cross-paragraph root/endpoint and similar material-account repetition remain; no claim of universal brevity or release readiness.

The top-reply survey avoids arbitrary weak later moves, but choosing the most instructive functional contrast among similarly strong replies remains limited. Some top replies can have the same observed continuation; no difference is invented.

verdict.bounded_goal: Met: shared root preparation -> useful action -> owned reply realization and necessary cost, verified in Kg2, Rf3 and the preregistered Re2.
verdict.general_explanatory_power: Partial: no claim to discover or rank all long-term ideas, explain every numerical evaluation, provide universal brevity or be release-ready.
verdict.evidence: The actual basic screens explain the causal plan and real response choices. Tests and added prose alone are not the completion criterion.
verdict.timing: Last jobs 6.18s, 8.03s and 6.05s under 10-second requests. A first Re2 job after the final survey change stopped at 10.01s; general first-run reliability remains unproven.
